description: CBE liberalises the exchange rate (float) with a non-binding guidance rate of 13; policy rates raised.
note: Before = fixed 8.8 (held since March 2016). After = guidance rate, not a market price. '48%' (Al Jazeera) and '32.3%' (Arab News) are the same move measured two ways.

description: Exceptional MPC meeting: +100 bp and a ~14% fall of the pound, citing the Ukraine war and foreign outflows.
note: FX values are the CBE buying rate. BusinessDay gives 18.17-18.27 for the day.

description: Pound falls ~14.5% as CBE commits to a durably flexible regime (+200 bp) and the IMF staff-level agreement ($3bn) is announced.
note: FX values are Refinitiv figures as reported (after is 'around 23'). The IMF page URL shows 26 Oct, the page header 27 Oct.

description: Sharp fall of the pound to a new low under the 'flexible regime' required by the IMF programme.
note: Values differ by source and time of day: 30 (CBE, morning), 31.95 (state banks), 29.7 (afternoon). After = 30.0. No policy-rate change was reported in these sources (left empty, not zero).

description: CBE lets the pound float freely and raises rates by 600 bp at an unscheduled meeting; the IMF programme is expanded to $8bn.
note: After = interbank close 49.60 (peak 50.70). Before not stated in the pages read. Sources disagree on the new deposit rate (27.25 vs 28.25), so rate levels are not stored.

description: Pound passes 52 per dollar for the first time (record low) as foreign investors leave local debt markets amid the regional war.
note: Market-driven, not an official devaluation: no policy change was reported. Date is Sunday 8 March (some notes say 9 March). Before = Thursday 5 March buying rate; after = Sunday buying close (52.15 on bank screens per The National).
